# Transformation observations

`transformation.tsv` records actual public transformation and direct `inheritTransformation` calls.
Source twice and the bundled JAR produce identical bytes.
The fixture contains 48 cases, 149 snapshots, and 101 explicit operations.
The shared [reproduction protocol](reproduction.README.md) defines construction, types, setup, and the comparison contract.

## Covered behavior

| Group | Actual source outcomes |
| --- | --- |
| Entry points | Public wrapper; direct first=true; direct first=false rejection. |
| Placement | Center success, all eight fallback directions, and fully blocked failure. |
| Identity filters | Default candidate ID zero, unrelated-parent exemption, equal IDs on distinct objects, and wrapped parent IDs. |
| Allocation | Real next-ID transition from maximum integer to minimum integer. |
| Velocity | Parent linear velocity transfer, zero candidate rotation, and no ordinary spore dispersal multiplier. |
| Energy | Parent energy subtraction only after placement; blocked and first=false cases preserve parent energy. |
| Accounting | Wrapper adds birth statistics without incrementing lifetime children or killing the victim. |
| Spores | Every modifier from one through twelve, without ordinary parent-version guards. |
| Adaptation | All six thresholds; both actual outcomes for each random gate. |
| Lineage | Increasing/decreasing genes and symmetry, marker limits, and equal-structure symmetry redraw. |
| Failed candidate | A real generated-NaN chain causes candidate death and retained statistics before placement fails. |

The helper selects fallback directions through bounded actual-source searches.
It observes resulting coordinates; it contains no placement formula.
Adaptation searches also inspect actual candidate activity.
The chosen seeds remain explicit inputs in final records.
Transformation generation uses 236 bounded-search attempts across its cases.

Gene-count and symmetry mutations cannot occur together in one inherited constructor.
Their source branches are mutually exclusive.
The original bounded search for that impossible combination failed and remains preserved.
Separate actual mutations cover both branches.

The equal-structure case first calls `inheritTransformation(false)` with a selected mutation seed.
Its rejected source candidate retains an update-clade flag despite equal gene count and symmetry.
The case then repeats that explicit seed through a successful first=true call.
The available result clears its lineage flag without adding a marker.
Rejected candidate internals remain separately disposed.

The generated-NaN case starts with a valid zero-length pasted parent.
It invokes actual grow, velocity offset, and forced bounds methods.
Direct transformation then creates a candidate that dies at the origin before placement fails.
Its genotype remains reachable through the actual last-dead statistics record.
That genotype stays `observable` and requires complete G/N comparisons.
This method sequence does not claim normal complete-frame scheduling.

## Direct candidate protocol

Direct calls add these rows to the shared protocol:

| Tag | Columns after the tag |
| --- | --- |
| `B` | Stage, `inheritTransformation`, actual boolean result. |
| `Z` | Stage, candidate role, `available` or `rejected` result scope. |

Direct candidates use `candidateN` roles and remain outside actual world membership.
Available candidates remain fully comparable through the Rust construction result.
Their actor fields, reference holders, queries, genotype values, and RNG effects remain acceptance observations.
Public wrapper children instead enter the real world list and receive D discovery rows.

Rejected direct candidates are retained only by the Java observer.
Rust returns no valid candidate object for these failures.
Preserve their O/H/Q rows without claiming passed Rust comparisons.
Continue comparing original actors, world effects, statistics, and RNG exactly.

Y classifies each actual genotype separately after each call.
It includes setup genomes, available actors, world members, and statistics references as observable roots.
A genotype reachable only through rejected observer candidates receives `rejected-only`.
Its G/N records remain preserved without a Rust comparison claim.

Do not exclude a genotype merely because its candidate was rejected.
The failed generated-NaN candidate demonstrates why statistics-root genotypes remain observable.
Do not replace rejected candidates with dummy organisms or use their observed genomes as constructor inputs.

Explicit operations comprise four wrapper transformations, 46 direct constructions, 48 tree builds, and three movement preparations.
Direct constructions return 42 available and four rejected candidates.
The observer retains five rejected actor views because one rejection remains visible across two snapshots.
Those views account for 790 O/H/Q dispositions.
Four private genotype views account for 512 G/N dispositions.
No global statistics-root genotype is discarded.

Transformation construction occupies `Organism.java:2534-2995`.
Center/fallback placement occupies `Organism.java:3467-3510`.
The public wrapper occupies `Organism.java:4160-4170`.
Collision exclusions occupy `World.java:700-712`; addition ordering occupies `World.java:747-756`.

The same serializer correction, preservation checks, isolated profiles, and negative guards apply to both fixture modes.
Their provenance records each backend command and compiled helper hash.
No full frame, contact integration, UI callback, save migration, or complete ecology acceptance follows from these observations.
Rust replay and integration results remain separate evidence.
